agent.label: About
agent.heading: Redefining how homes are shown.
body: I'm Jana. For nine years I've sold homes in Barcelona, and I film every one of them before it goes near a portal.

Photographs are chosen. A film is the whole flat - every room, in natural light, start to finish. You decide from the film, so nobody wastes a Saturday being polite. By the time we meet at the door, the conversation is already serious.

steps.title: I call within 24 hours

steps.title: We view, privately
steps.body: Around your schedule, usually within 48 hours. No open houses, no crowds.

items.q: What does it cost me as a buyer?
items.a: Nothing to me. The seller pays the commission. You pay the purchase price, the taxes and your own legal fees, and I'll give you a written breakdown before you commit to anything.

items.q: What are the extra costs on top of the price?
items.a: Transfer tax, notary, land registry, gestoría and your own lawyer all sit on top of the asking price. The exact figure depends on the property, so I give you a written breakdown for the specific home rather than a rule of thumb.

items.q: Can I buy in Spain as a non-resident?
items.a: Yes. You will need an NIE and a Spanish bank account, both of which take days rather than weeks. I work with a gestor and an independent lawyer who handle this routinely.
I don't broker them, but I'll introduce you to independent brokers who lend to non-residents. You're free to use your own.

items.q: How quickly can I see a home?
items.a: Usually within 48 hours, weekends included. If you're flying in, tell me your dates and I'll group viewings into a single day.

items.q: Are these all the properties you have?
items.a: No. What is filmed and published here is a fraction of it: there are over 300 exclusive properties on my books and most never reach a portal. Tell me what you are after on the call.

items.q: Is the home really like the film?
items.a: That is the point. One take, no staging, natural light. Anything wrong with it is in the film too.
